messages:
jamie: Heads-up — POC customer (FinEdge) is seeing intermittent connection resets and spurious 429s when the app sits behind their corporate HTTP proxy. Repro in both our TS and Python SDKs. Root trace attached, but quick question: could HTTP/2 connection reuse + proxy pipelining be tripping our gateway?

carmen: Can you paste the minimal error log? is it 429 or a stream error?

jamie: Logs: 
```
ERROR: request failed: stream error: PROTOCOL_ERROR
WARN: transient 429 from inference.redwood.prod (x-retry-after: 1)
INFO: client retry attempt 2 -> conn reset
```
Also seen: `net::ERR_HTTP2_PROTOCOL_ERROR` in browser devtools. Customer says their proxy modifies headers for large streaming responses.

alex: Seen similar when proxies rewrite `:scheme` or drop `transfer-encoding`. Quick repro step: force curl to use HTTP/1.1 and check if the issue stops. e.g. 
```
curl -v --http1.1 -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{"input": "hi"}' https://api.redwood.run/v1/generate
```
If that avoids the error, it's most likely an h2/proxy edge case.

jamie: Tried that — forcing http/1.1 via curl removes the PROTOCOL_ERROR and 429s disappear. Customer can't permanently switch their proxy behavior though. Any SDK-level mitigations?

alex: Two options we typically recommend for POC:
- SDK toggle: force HTTP/1.1 for requests to our API (node: set `fetch` to use http/1.1 via curl fallback or set env var in our SDK).
- Connection tuning: reduce connection reuse and set conservative keepalive/idle timeouts so the proxy doesn't reuse stale streams.

Example TS workaround (in their app) — forcing HTTP/1.1 by using a direct fetch wrapper or proxying through a small sidecar that speaks HTTP/1.1 to us: 
```ts
// pseudo-code for the quick POC workaround
import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference';
const client = new RedwoodClient({
  transportOptions: {
    forceHttp1: true,       // SDK-level short-term toggle
    timeoutMs: 30000,
    retry: { retries: 3, backoffMs: 200 }
  }
});
```

python workaround: use `requests`/`httpx` forcing http1 by avoiding httpx/http2 plugin or using `curl` adapter.

kevin: Eng-runtime note — we did see a small cluster of PROTOCOL_ERRORs ~2 weeks ago after a proxy vendor pushed a change. Gateway will continue to support HTTP/2, but we can add a targeted workaround: expose an env/config flag in the SDK to force HTTP/1.1 for affected customers. I'll open an eng ticket. For the POC now, recommend the SDK toggle + increase server-side idle window for the customer's tenant for 24h.

jamie: Thanks. Customer also asked about whether this impacts pricing or SLAs for the POC — they hit extra retries so token counts increased. Any short guidance on credits/discounts for noise?

carmen: For POC we can offer to off-set obvious retry noise. I'll coordinate with sales ops to apply a small credit and note it in the contract addendum. Please capture approximate extra token count and time range.

jamie: Will do. For the engineer side, I'll: 1) give them the forceHttp1 workaround; 2) send a tcpdump snippet request; 3) share the timeout/retry snippet.

deploy-bot: New ticket created: ENG-9821 — investigate h2/proxy PROTOCOL_ERROR and add SDK toggle. Assigned to kevin.

alex: One more tip — if they must keep proxy h2, try disabling HTTP/2 multiplexing on the proxy or set max concurrent streams lower. That often avoids pipeline head-of-line issues.

jamie: Solid. I'll push the workaround into their POC branch now and update this thread with results. :thumbsup:
